ei.title: The Subscription Economy: From Ownership to Access
ei.subject: 영어2

fullPassage: Jiyun, a high school student, starts her day by logging in to a music streaming service on her smartphone. She enjoys listening to her favorite music, discovering new songs, and exploring new artists every day. For a healthy breakfast, Jiyun receives a delivery from a subscription service that provides fresh vegetables and fruits. After school, Jiyun utilizes a video lecture service to expand her knowledge in whatever she finds interesting. For example, she watches various academic lectures to review her schoolwork and stay updated about the latest knowledge in her chosen field of study. During weekends, Jiyun and her family spend quality time together watching movies or dramas using a streaming service. Subscriptions are everywhere To be sure, the subscription economy is a popular economic model nowadays, and Jiyun is actively taking part in it. The concept of business models based on subscriptions is not new. Initially it was limited to products such as milk and newspapers. However, these business models have expanded to all industries, including entertainment, technology, fashion, education, and much more. Instead of creating a hit product that will be sold once, companies now prioritize providing continuing value, such as new content, more personalization, or access to updates. Customers pay for these benefits via a regular subscription. The subscription economy brings advantages for both companies and consumers. Companies can have a stable revenue and build customer loyalty by using the subscription model. From the consumers’ perspective, they can enjoy a wider range of choices and personalized experiences. They can also save money by having flexible subscription contracts. The rise of the subscription economy is closely connected to two major drivers: changes in consumption trends and the rapid growth of online platforms. People love the subscriptions The subscription economy is highly relevant to how people consume goods and services nowadays. More and more people prioritize experiences over owning things. This makes the subscription economy attractive to them because it offers access to services or content without the requirement of ownership. For example, by subscribing to a music streaming service, consumers can enjoy limitless music without the need for having disc albums. Another example is subscribing to clothing services, where consumers can explore a variety of clothing styles without filling up their drawers. Moreover, consumers value diversity and customization. The subscription economy offers a diverse range of subscription options, enabling individuals to personalize their experiences based on their own preferences and interests. This aspect of the subscription economy is more popular among younger generations, as they enjoy expressing their uniqueness and discovering valuable content and services that fit with their individual tastes. A popular example that has gained attention is the cosmetics subscription service. It stands out by thoroughly analyzing customers’ current skin conditions and providing specialized recommendations, including manufacturing cosmetics created to address each individual’s unique skin concerns. To come to the point, consumers receive a personalized experience that prioritizes their individual skin conditions, rather than a uniform purchasing process. Furthermore, consumers appreciate flexibility and convenience. In some subscription models, consumers can experience a variety of products or services for a fixed cost. In other models, they can flexibly adjust subscription fees by choosing only the necessary services or products when needed. This means they can either enjoy a range of offerings for a set price or save money by selecting only what they really need. Moreover, subscription services are made easily accessible by online platforms, enhancing consumers’ convenience. With just a few clicks, consumers can receive services or products. If they wish to change their device model, they can do so. Whoever desires an upgrade can get it and experience the latest models. Online platforms drive the subscription economy With the development of various digital devices centered on smartphones, consumers have been able to do numerous things with great ease. In the past, people had no choice but to go to the theater or purchase the videos they wanted to watch. Today, whoever wants to watch a movie can access online media subscription platforms and enjoy a vast selection of movies on their smartphones or other digital devices. At the same time, these platforms make it easy for companies to offer customized products and services to customers. By applying AI and big data algorithm technology, companies identify consumers’ needs, tastes, and consumption patterns. People appreciate having diverse choices and customization, which in turn enhances their satisfaction. Services, such as suggesting personalized clothing styles based on customers’ purchase history or recommending videos that match their movie and video viewing history, bring them great satisfaction. Limitations of the subscription economy Although the subscription economy offers many advantages, there are also some disadvantages to consider. One concern is the potential for overconsumption. The convenience and accessibility of the subscription model make it easy for consumers to sign up for multiple services and use a lot of content or products. This can result in excessive consumption and using more subscription services than actually needed. It is crucial to subscribe only to services that are truly necessary and avoid subscribing to similar services. Related to the concern of overconsumption is the financial burden that subscriptions can create. While the cost of individual subscriptions may seem affordable, subscribing to multiple services can add up quickly. It is important to carefully consider the costs of these subscriptions to avoid financial strain. Regularly reviewing and canceling unnecessary subscriptions can be beneficial. Additionally, the subscription economy can contribute to environmental pollution. The regular delivery of products in packaging materials can increase the use of disposable packaging, which harms the environment. Using environmentally friendly packaging materials and opting for reusable packaging can help reduce this problem. Despite the potential limitations of subscription services, they have become deeply embedded in our lives and more and more businesses are jumping onto the subscription economy model. It is expected that new subscription services will be continuously provided to consumers in new areas in the future. We need to have a deeper understanding of the subscription economy and become wise consumers who receive the services that are really needed.

questions.passage: Online platforms drive the subscription economy With the development of various digital devices centered on smartphones, consumers ①<u>has been able</u> to do numerous things with great ease.  In the past, people had no choice but to go to the theater or ②<u>purchase</u> the videos they wanted to watch.  Today, whoever wants to watch a movie can access online media subscription platforms and enjoy a vast selection of movies on their smartphones or other digital devices.  At the same time, these platforms make it easy for companies to offer customized products and services to customers.  ③<u>By applying</u> AI and big data algorithm technology, companies identify consumers’ needs, tastes, and consumption patterns.  People appreciate having diverse choices and customization, which in turn ④<u>enhances</u> their satisfaction.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① has been able → have been able
det.analysis:
❌ ① has been able → have been able: 주어가 복수 명사 consumers(소비자들)라서 복수형 have가 맞아요. 단수 has는 틀려요 ← 정답

✅ ② purchase: 'go to the theater or purchase the videos'에서 앞의 go와 or로 이어지는 동사원형이라 적절해요.

✅ ③ By applying: 'By applying AI and big data technology'에서 전치사 By 뒤에 동명사(-ing)라 적절해요.

✅ ④ enhances: 'customization, which in turn enhances their satisfaction'에서 which가 받는 것이 단수 개념이라 단수 동사 enhances가 적절해요.
det.tip: 복수 주어 consumers → have been able.

questions.passage: This aspect of the subscription economy is more popular among younger generations, as they enjoy expressing their uniqueness and discovering valuable content and services that fit with their individual tastes.  A popular example that has gained attention is the cosmetics subscription service.  It stands out by thoroughly ①<u>analyzing</u> customers’ current skin conditions and providing specialized recommendations, including ②<u>manufacture</u> cosmetics created ③<u>to address</u> each individual’s unique skin concerns.  To come to the point, consumers receive a personalized experience that ④<u>prioritizes</u> their individual skin conditions, rather than a uniform purchasing process.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① analyzing: 'by thoroughly analyzing customers' current skin conditions'에서 전치사 by 뒤 동명사(-ing)라 적절해요.

❌ ② manufacture → manufacturing: 'including manufacturing cosmetics'에서 including은 전치사처럼 쓰여 뒤에 동명사(-ing)가 와야 해요. 그래서 manufacturing이 맞고 manufacture는 틀려요 ← 정답

✅ ③ to address: 'cosmetics created to address each individual's skin concerns'에서 목적(~하기 위해)을 나타내는 to부정사라 적절해요.

✅ ④ prioritizes: 'a personalized experience that prioritizes their skin conditions'에서 that이 받는 것이 단수 experience라서 단수 동사 prioritizes가 적절해요.
det.tip: 전치사 including 뒤에는 동명사: including manufacturing.

questions.passage: However, these business models have expanded to all industries, ①<u>including</u> entertainment, technology, fashion, education, and much more.  Instead of creating a hit product that ②<u>will be sold</u> once, companies now prioritize ③<u>provide</u> continuing value, such as new content, more personalization, or access to updates.  Customers ④<u>pay</u> for these benefits via a regular subscription.  The subscription economy brings advantages for both companies and consumers.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① including: 'expanded to all industries, including entertainment'에서 예를 덧붙이는 including이라 적절해요.

✅ ② will be sold: 'a hit product that will be sold once'에서 상품은 '팔리는' 대상이라 미래 수동태(will be + p.p.)가 적절해요.

❌ ③ provide → providing: 'companies now prioritize ___ continuing value'에서 동사 prioritize의 목적어 자리라 동명사(-ing)가 와야 해요. 그래서 providing이 맞고 provide는 틀려요 ← 정답

✅ ④ pay: 'Customers pay for these benefits'에서 복수 주어 Customers에 맞는 동사라 적절해요.
det.tip: prioritize + 동명사(providing): ~을 제공하는 것을 우선하다.

questions.passage: Related to the concern of overconsumption is the financial ①<u>burden</u> that subscriptions can create.  While the cost of individual subscriptions may seem affordable, subscribing to multiple services can add up quickly.  It is important to carefully consider the costs of these subscriptions to avoid financial ②<u>strain</u>.  Regularly reviewing and canceling unnecessary subscriptions can be beneficial.  Additionally, the subscription economy can ③<u>contribute</u> to environmental pollution.  The regular delivery of products in packaging materials can increase the use of ④<u>reusable</u> packaging, which harms the environment.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① burden: 'the financial burden that subscriptions can create'에서 과소비로 생기는 '재정적 부담'이라는 문맥에 적절해요.

✅ ② strain: 'to avoid financial strain'에서 재정적 '압박'을 피한다는 문맥에 적절해요.

✅ ③ contribute: 'the subscription economy can contribute to environmental pollution'에서 환경오염에 '일조한다'는 문맥에 적절해요.

❌ ④ reusable → disposable: 'increase the use of ___ packaging, which harms the environment'에서 환경에 해를 끼치는 것은 '일회용(disposable)' 포장재예요. '재사용(reusable)' 포장재는 오히려 해를 줄이므로 반대라 부적절해요 ← 정답
det.tip: 환경에 해를 끼침 → disposable(일회용) ↔ reusable(재사용)은 반대.

questions.passage: She enjoys listening to her ①<u>boring</u> music, discovering new songs, and exploring new artists every day.  For a healthy breakfast, Jiyun receives a delivery from a subscription service that provides ②<u>fresh</u> vegetables and fruits.  After school, Jiyun utilizes a video lecture service to ③<u>expand</u> her knowledge in whatever she finds interesting.  For example, she watches various academic lectures to ④<u>review</u> her schoolwork and stay updated about the latest knowledge in her chosen field of study.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① boring → favorite: 'She enjoys listening to her ___ music'에서 지윤이 음악을 '즐긴다'고 했으니 '가장 좋아하는(favorite)' 음악이 맞아요. '지루한(boring)'은 즐긴다는 흐름과 반대라 부적절해요 ← 정답

✅ ② fresh: 'provides fresh vegetables and fruits'에서 '신선한' 채소와 과일이라는 문맥에 적절해요.

✅ ③ expand: 'to expand her knowledge'에서 강의로 지식을 '넓힌다'는 문맥에 적절해요.

✅ ④ review: 'to review her schoolwork'에서 배운 것을 '복습한다'는 문맥에 적절해요.
det.tip: 즐겨 듣는 음악 → favorite(가장 좋아하는) ↔ boring(지루한)은 반대.

questions.passage: The subscription economy brings advantages for __________.  Companies can have a stable revenue and build customer loyalty by using the subscription model.  From the consumers’ perspective, they can enjoy a wider range of choices and personalized experiences.  They can also save money by having flexible subscription contracts.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸: both companies and consumers (기업과 소비자 모두)
det.analysis:
❌ ① only large corporations(대기업만): 소비자 쪽 이점도 이어지므로 '기업만'은 틀려요.

✅ ② both companies and consumers(기업과 소비자 모두): 빈칸 뒤에서 기업의 이점(안정적 수익)과 소비자의 이점(더 넓은 선택)을 나란히 설명하므로 '양쪽 모두'가 맞아요 ← 정답

❌ ③ government agencies(정부 기관): 본문에 정부 이야기는 없어요.

❌ ④ foreign investors(외국인 투자자): 본문과 무관해요.
det.tip: 뒤 문장이 기업 이점 + 소비자 이점을 모두 다뤄요 → both.

questions.passage: Moreover, subscription services are made easily accessible by online platforms, enhancing consumers’ convenience.  With just a few clicks, consumers can receive services or products.  If they wish to change their device model, they can do so.  Whoever desires an upgrade can get it and experience __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① a full refund(전액 환불): 환불 이야기가 아니에요.

❌ ② a paper manual(종이 설명서): 문맥과 무관해요.

✅ ③ the latest models(최신 모델): 빈칸 앞에서 '업그레이드를 원하는 사람은 누구나 그것을 얻을 수 있다'고 했으므로, '최신 모델'을 경험할 수 있다는 뜻이 맞아요 ← 정답

❌ ④ a free ticket(무료 입장권): 문맥과 맞지 않아요.
det.tip: desires an upgrade(업그레이드를 원함) → experience the latest models(최신 모델 경험).

questions.passage: Jiyun, a high school student, starts her day by logging in to a music streaming service on her smartphone.  She enjoys listening to her favorite music, discovering new songs, and exploring new artists every day.  For a healthy breakfast, Jiyun receives a delivery from a subscription service that provides fresh vegetables and fruits.  After school, Jiyun utilizes a video lecture service to expand her knowledge in whatever she finds interesting.  For example, she watches various academic lectures to review her schoolwork and stay updated about the latest knowledge in her chosen field of study.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① 본문 'Jiyun utilizes a video lecture service to expand her knowledge in whatever she finds interesting'과 일치해요.

✅ ② 본문 'starts her day by logging in to a music streaming service on her smartphone'과 일치해요.

✅ ③ 본문 'Jiyun and her family spend quality time together watching movies or dramas using a streaming service'와 일치해요.

❌ ④ 본문 'Jiyun receives a delivery from a subscription service that provides fresh vegetables and fruits'에서 채소·과일은 '구독 서비스로 배송받는다'고 했어요. '직접 시장에 가서 사 온다'는 반대라 불일치 ← 정답
det.tip: receives a delivery(배송받음) ↔ 직접 사 오기는 반대예요.

ch: 지윤은 방과 후에 동영상 강의 서비스를 이용해 관심 분야의 지식을 넓힌다.
지윤은 스마트폰의 음악 스트리밍 서비스에 로그인하며 하루를 시작한다.
지윤은 주말에 가족과 함께 스트리밍 서비스로 영화나 드라마를 본다.
지윤은 건강한 아침 식사를 위해 직접 시장에 가서 채소와 과일을 사 온다.

questions.passage: Subscriptions are everywhere To be sure, the subscription economy is a popular economic model nowadays, and Jiyun is actively taking part in it.  The concept of business models based on subscriptions is not new.  Initially it was limited to products such as milk and newspapers. questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① 본문 'Initially it was limited to products such as milk and newspapers. However, these business models have expanded to all industries'와 일치해요 ← 정답

❌ ② 본문 'The concept ... is not new'에서 새로운 개념이 아니라고 했어요.

❌ ③ 본문 'Instead of creating a hit product that will be sold once, companies now prioritize providing continuing value'에서 오히려 '지속적 가치'를 우선한다고 했어요.

❌ ④ 본문 'Customers pay for these benefits via a regular subscription'에서 '정기 구독'으로 결제한다고 했으니 '한 번만'은 틀려요.
det.tip: milk and newspapers에서 시작 → all industries로 expanded(확장).

ch: 구독 사업 모델은 우유와 신문 같은 제품에서 시작해 여러 산업으로 확장되었다.
구독 사업 모델은 최근에야 처음 생긴 완전히 새로운 개념이다.
기업들은 한 번 팔고 마는 히트 상품 하나를 만드는 데에만 집중한다.
고객은 여러 혜택에 대해 처음 한 번만 결제하면 된다.

questions.passage: Additionally, the subscription economy can contribute to environmental pollution.  The regular delivery of products in packaging materials can increase the use of disposable packaging, which harms the environment.  Using environmentally friendly packaging materials and opting for reusable packaging can help reduce this problem. It is expected that new subscription services will be continuously provided to consumers in new areas in the future.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① 본문 'The regular delivery of products in packaging materials can increase the use of disposable packaging, which harms the environment'과 일치해요.

❌ ② 본문 'they have become deeply embedded in our lives and more and more businesses are jumping onto the subscription economy model'에서 구독 서비스는 오히려 삶에 깊이 자리 잡았다고 했어요. '점차 사라지고 있다'는 반대라 불일치 ← 정답

✅ ③ 본문 'Using environmentally friendly packaging materials and opting for reusable packaging can help reduce this problem'과 일치해요.

✅ ④ 본문 'It is expected that new subscription services will be continuously provided to consumers in new areas in the future'와 일치해요.
det.tip: deeply embedded(깊이 자리 잡음) + businesses jumping on → 사라지는 게 아니에요.

ch: 정기적인 제품 배송은 일회용 포장재 사용을 늘려 환경에 해를 끼칠 수 있다.
구독 서비스는 여러 한계 때문에 사람들의 삶에서 점차 사라지고 있다.
친환경 포장재를 쓰고 재사용 포장을 택하면 이 문제를 줄이는 데 도움이 된다.
앞으로 새로운 구독 서비스가 새로운 분야에서 계속 제공될 것으로 예상된다.

questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① 온라인 쇼핑 할인법은 글의 소재가 아니에요.

questions.passage: Subscriptions are everywhere To be sure, the subscription economy is a popular economic model nowadays, and Jiyun is actively taking part in it.  The concept of business models based on subscriptions is not new.  Initially it was limited to products such as milk and newspapers.  However, these business models have expanded to all industries, including entertainment, technology, fashion, education, and much more.  Instead of creating a hit product that will be sold once, companies now prioritize providing continuing value, such as new content, more personalization, or access to updates.  Customers pay for these benefits via a regular subscription.  The subscription economy brings advantages for both companies and consumers.  Companies can have a stable revenue and build customer loyalty by using the subscription model.  From the consumers’ perspective, they can enjoy a wider range of choices and personalized experiences.  They can also save money by having flexible subscription contracts.  The rise of the subscription economy is closely connected to two major drivers: changes in consumption trends and the rapid growth of online platforms.  People love the subscriptions The subscription economy is highly relevant to how people consume goods and services nowadays.  More and more people prioritize experiences over owning things.  This makes the subscription economy attractive to them because it offers access to services or content without the requirement of ownership.  For example, by subscribing to a music streaming service, consumers can enjoy limitless music without the need for having disc albums.  Another example is subscribing to clothing services, where consumers can explore a variety of clothing styles without filling up their drawers.  Moreover, consumers value diversity and customization.  The subscription economy offers a diverse range of subscription options, enabling individuals to personalize their experiences based on their own preferences and interests.  This aspect of the subscription economy is more popular among younger generations, as they enjoy expressing their uniqueness and discovering valuable content and services that fit with their individual tastes.  A popular example that has gained attention is the cosmetics subscription service.  It stands out by thoroughly analyzing customers’ current skin conditions and providing specialized recommendations, including manufacturing cosmetics created to address each individual’s unique skin concerns.  To come to the point, consumers receive a personalized experience that prioritizes their individual skin conditions, rather than a uniform purchasing process.  Furthermore, consumers appreciate flexibility and convenience.  In some subscription models, consumers can experience a variety of products or services for a fixed cost.  In other models, they can flexibly adjust subscription fees by choosing only the necessary services or products when needed.  This means they can either enjoy a range of offerings for a set price or save money by selecting only what they really need.  Moreover, subscription services are made easily accessible by online platforms, enhancing consumers’ convenience.  With just a few clicks, consumers can receive services or products.  If they wish to change their device model, they can do so.  Whoever desires an upgrade can get it and experience the latest models.  Online platforms drive the subscription economy With the development of various digital devices centered on smartphones, consumers have been able to do numerous things with great ease.  In the past, people had no choice but to go to the theater or purchase the videos they wanted to watch.  Today, whoever wants to watch a movie can access online media subscription platforms and enjoy a vast selection of movies on their smartphones or other digital devices.  At the same time, these platforms make it easy for companies to offer customized products and services to customers.  By applying AI and big data algorithm technology, companies identify consumers’ needs, tastes, and consumption patterns.  People appreciate having diverse choices and customization, which in turn enhances their satisfaction.  Services, such as suggesting personalized clothing styles based on customers’ purchase history or recommending videos that match their movie and video viewing history, bring them great satisfaction.
